_readme: How an agent's own task comment says so, in a way the agent can recognise when it
reads the board back. Compiled by agents/agent-comment.mjs and design/agent_comment.py
from these very strings, so the two languages cannot drift — the same reason
comment-grammar.json exists, and the drift it prevents is worse here: a marker the
reader fails to recognise turns the agent's own status note into a teammate's
instruction.
WHY A MARKER AND NOT THE AUTHOR. Until 2026-09-18 a comment carried
`createdByAssistant` and the server said who wrote it. That field is gone; a comment
is now attributed to the owner of the API key that posted it. A deployment whose
agents run under a human's key — measured to be every key in this fleet, and the
default for anyone installing the pack, since NOAN has no service accounts — cannot
tell its own comments from that person's by author alone. So the comment says it
itself.
FAIL-SAFE BY SHAPE, VERIFIED BY SIGNATURE. Recognition is the shape of the
signature line, NOT whether the HMAC checks out. The two failure directions are not
symmetric: an unrecognised agent comment is read as human steering (dangerous), while
a wrongly-recognised human comment is merely dropped (annoying). Shape-matching fails
in the harmless direction even when the secret is missing or rotated, which a
verify-to-recognise rule would not. The HMAC's job is to catch tampering and config
drift and say so loudly — not to gate recognition.
AN UNSIGNED COMMENT IS STILL A MARKED COMMENT. Where no secret is configured the
signature reads `unsigned` and the line is still written, because the alternative —
emitting no line at all — makes an agent comment UNRECOGNISABLE, which is the
dangerous direction the shape rule exists to avoid. The first cut of this file got
that wrong: it failed safe on a WRONG secret but not on a MISSING one.
The signature binds the body AND the task id, so a comment copied onto another task
no longer verifies. A verbatim replay onto the SAME task still verifies, which is
harmless: it is classified as the agent's own and ignored.
Patterns use only syntax both engines read identically: (?:...), \s, \n, [0-9a-f].
No named groups, no lookbehind.
_label_note: Prepended as a first line, '<AGENT_NAME>· agent status', so a human reading the
board can see who wrote it. Necessary because creator.name now shows the key
owner's name — a person's name — on every agent comment.
The agent's name comes from AGENT_NAME at call time, never a literal here.

sign._payload_note: HMAC over taskId + "\n" + body, where body is the comment text with the signature line and trailing whitespace removed.
